VRAM permanently occupied 23471/24564 MiB (processes /strata + /strata-vision). Speculative decoding MTP=4 + lookup=3, pcie_frac 0.35, image input enabled, one request at a time. WSL2 is not an officially documented path: RAM must be allocated via .wslconfig (96 GB here) or the engine can't load the 35-55 GB of experts. 4x32GB double-rank DDR4 holding 3600 CL18 (unusual on Ryzen 5000 - most boards drop to 3200 with this many ranks), so the RAM-resident experts get ~57 GB/s of dual-channel bandwidth. | dedicated Qwen3.8-Flash-Next engine, OpenAI/Anthropic API Hi, Please note that big parts of this post have been written with the help of the hereafter described model using OpenWork harness as I was afraid to miss relevant infos Strata on a 4090 + 128 GB, under WSL2 — agentic coding Direct answer to @lhl (post #25): yes, Strata changes the “small GPU” equation. A Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B in IQ3_S runs on a single 4090 here, at ~108 tok/s decode in real agent use. Beyond raw speed, what sold me is the prompt cache: ~90% hit rate, so agent follow-ups on ~50k-token contexts resume in 0.3-0.8 s instead of re-prefilling. One note for anyone eyeing WSL2: the docs target native Windows or native Linux. Under WSL2 you must allocate RAM explicitly (.wslconfig, 96 GB here - WSL2 defaults to 50% of host), otherwise the engine doesn’t have enough RAM to load the 35-55 GB of experts. I came from llama.cpp (Qwen3.8-27B-UD-IQ4_X@256k, KV q4_0), where I was already doing very good agentic coding with Claude Code or Copilot CLI (both via VSCode terminal). No formal comparison, but Strata at IQ3_S/131k doesn’t make me miss the 27B at 256k - I do miss some context depth, and I’m planning to test 256k under Strata. On the tier brackets: with hybrid offload engines (Strata), the VRAM tier alone no longer describes what actually fits - this 125B IQ3_S run is RAM+SSD-bound, not VRAM-bound. A RAM column or an “hybrid/offload” flag would be more honest than a VRAM bracket. Cheers !

submissions.notes: chat profile, 1 slot, 5781 expert slots / 11 GB VRAM; ~88% of all input tokens served from KV reuse across the 3291-request log, ~99% per turn inside a growing live session; vision .mmproj unchanged (1024 image tokens); supersedes the 131k part of my Oct 12 entry Follow-up: 256k context on the same 4090 rig — and why I now run two launch profiles Hi again — my Oct 12 post said I was planning to try 256k under Strata. I did, and TL;DR: decode barely moved, prefill latency is the real cost, and 262k forced me into two launch profiles. (Still hybrid — glad to see the matrix grew a flag for it.) The numbers, from the engine log: 3,291 requests, 95 boots, Oct 7 → 25. Decode filtered to requests generating ≥128 tokens: decode p25 / median / p75 — 131k: 92 / 103 / 113 · 262k one stream: 95 / 101 / 107 · 262k two streams: 52 / 55 / 59 prefill median (>=8k fresh tokens) — ~3480 tok/s at 131k · ~3460 single-stream · ~1720 two streams expert cache in VRAM — 6400-7700 slots (12-14.6 GB) at 131k · 5781 (11.0 GB) single-stream · 1786 (3.4 GB) two streams Longest live session: 228,553 tokens — 65 s cold prefill (~3.5k tok/s), then 101 tok/s decode. Zero OOM, zero context-full errors, zero coherence collapse across the whole log. Vision still fine at 262k (same .mmproj, stress-tested at 2x context). The real cost is prefill latency, not throughput. Per-token prefill speed didn’t change at all; the cold-cache wall-clock roughly doubled: ~65 s for a 228k prompt vs ~35 s at 131k. That delay on cache misses is what pushed me into prompt caching. Why two launch profiles: at 262k the int8 KV eats ~3.6 GB of VRAM per slot, so 2 streams starve the expert cache (5781 → 1786 slots ≈ 70 % of experts pushed to RAM) and decode drops to ~55 tok/s. So I pick chat (1 stream, full expert cache — my default) or agentic (2 streams, roughly half TG). Claude Code on the agentic profile kept KV reuse at 86 % and sessions at 201k tokens across both slots — it works, but the fan-out didn’t offset the TG drop. Back-to-131k A/B matched my gut almost exactly — TG identical, 262k only slower on cold prefill. Subjective bonus at 256k: fewer auto-compactions in Claude Code, and long OpenWork conversations stay coherent over more turns (impression, not a metric). KV variant benches (same day, one fixed prompt: ~10k fresh tokens forced cold with a unique salt, then 900 decoded): single-stream chat, k8v4 changes nothing (5636 → 6011 experts, ~99 tok/s either way). Under agentic load it does: experts 1620 → 2878, decode per stream 28.8/24.1 → 34.1/28.5 tok/s, prefill 1560 → 1925 — reproduced on an A/B reversal. Caveats: those decode figures are fresh conversations (adapted sessions reach the ~55 above), and speculation served only one of the two streams in every pass, all three variants. (Sidenote) Forcing KV streaming under WSL2. The 3.6 GB-per-slot KV made me try --kv-resident 32768 — keep the hot KV window in VRAM (32,768 positions per layer), the rest in host RAM. Strata normally refuses that under WSL2; injected via user_args it ran: 255k-token request, 3602 prefill / 104.7 decode tok/s — no collapse over WSL’s ~26 GB/s PCIe — with 7257 experts in the freed VRAM. The log explains why: pinning works (cudaHostRegister PORTABLE ok) and 97 %+ of KV block reads still hit VRAM, locality keeping the working set inside the window. Even two-stream agentic benefits: 6343 experts, 40-52 tok/s decode. Daily driver still int8; native Win11 stays on the bench. raw.hardware: AMD Epyc 7543 (Milan, 32C/64T), LXC container with 128GB of RAM (no GPU)
raw.primary_use_case: Coding, and long form reasoning beyond what Gemma4:26B is capable of
raw.setup_notes: I tend to refine my coding prompts using Gemma4:26B, and then copy and paste the plan for the coding into Laguna and have it run in the background or overnight. Needed to tweak some settings to make the model run better on the CPU. Setting "PARAMETER num_batch 512" significantly improved performance. Pre-fill will always run very slowly on CPU's, which is what makes this more of an offline prompt model. The only reason this is usable at all for eval is because this is an enterprise server with 8x memory channels of DDR4-3200 each. On consumer hardware with only two memory channels this would be slow as molasses.
